candidate: Lessig DEIG causal-deaths premise, not yet an admitted issue

read_extent.author: All four physical pages, including hearing cover, complete medical text and bibliography. Extraction has OCR defects; no original quote transcribed in this review.
read_extent.primary: Original PubMed Zipes2012 record: entire abstract, methods/results/conclusion and correction/comment metadata; original Johns Hopkins coauthor-deposited Kunz2018 abstract and metadata; original AHA correction search extract. No full eight-case clinical appraisal or complete2018review claimed.

assessment: The original2012 study advances an affirmative causal mechanism from eight detailed clinical/legal cases; this is more than a press tally. But the2018 review actually cited by Lessig expressly takes the contrary position that no proven electrocution incidents are known. Existence of the contrary case report does not alone settle disputed causality.

The2012 correction narrows the prior-health description and first-ECG description, while preserving the author’s conclusion. The correction does not refute the entire study; equally its survival does not make the later contrary expert conclusion an established factual error.

Lessig acknowledges cardiac disease, stress, oxygen shortage, severe complications, vulnerable body regions and falls. His known-causal-deaths sentence should not be broadened to an assertion that no post-DEIG deaths or no contrary causal publications exist.

The four pages do not clearly request authorisation or blanket endorsement of DEIG. The explicit recommendations concern ECG, medical monitoring, documentation and ordinary operating instructions with rare-complication warnings. A favourable direction toward a broader statutory authorisation cannot be inferred solely from testimony in that hearing.
limits: Medical specialist review would be needed for a clinical-causality conclusion; no author intent inferred. Existing source disagreement and lack of a clear request link preclude a promoted error on this brief check.
